<a id="book"></a>

## Book: book (BOOK)

A trading book: owner desk, trades and risk. One row per book per business date, keyed by BOOK_ID. Read by the **core** pack's connector `reference-store` (table `<root>/reference/book/`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (30 records); each later day's file holds only the records new or changed that day (30–30 a day). Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 1,800 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/core/book/` + `book.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `BOOK_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 1,800 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json

  "BOOK_ID": "BOOK-COMM-1",
  "NAME": "Commodities · book 1",
  "DESK_NAME": "Commodities",

  "MTM": -148106150,
  "DV01": 0,
  "TOP_TRADES": [
    {
      "TRADE_ID": "1003930",

      "PRODUCT": "ENGY-SWAP",

      "CURRENCY": "USD",
      "BOOK": "BOOK-COMM-1",
      "NOTIONAL": 10199198808.0,
      "MATURITY": "2028-03-31",
      "MATURITY_BUCKET": "1-2Y",
      "MTM": -120455169
    },
    {
      "TRADE_ID": "1000098",
      "STATUS": "AMENDED",
      "PRODUCT": "ENGY-SWAP",
      "ASSET_CLASS": "Commodity",
      "CURRENCY": "USD",
      "BOOK": "BOOK-COMM-1",
      "NOTIONAL": 5640972613.63,
      "MATURITY": "2029-05-31",
      "MATURITY_BUCKET": "2-5Y",
      "MTM": -120728296
    },
    "… 8 more elements of the same shape"
  ],

  "REGULATORY_BOOK": "Trading book",

```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BOOK_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^BOOK-`; links to `path-book` | `"BOOK-COMM-1"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The book's display name: its desk's name and the book's number (Commodities · book 1). | — | `"Commodities · book 1"` |
| `DESK_NAME` | string | required | The name of the desk the book sits under (the desk's NAME). | — | `"Commodities"` |
| `TRADE_COUNT` | integer | required | How many trades are booked in the book. | — | `1000` |
| `MTM` | integer | required | The sum of the MTM of the book's trades, in the bank's reporting currency (USD in the demo). | unit: USD | `-148106150` |
| `DV01` | integer | required | The sum of the DV01 of the book's trades: the change in value for a one basis point rise in rates, in the bank's reporting currency (USD in the demo) per bp; negative loses when rates rise. | unit: USD per bp | `0` |
| `TOP_TRADES` | array of objects | required | The book's largest trades by absolute MTM, at most ten: one object per trade, largest first. | — | [10 objects] |
| `TOP_TRADES[].TRADE_ID` | string | required | The trade: a TRADE_ID of the trading pack's trade kind (text). | pattern `^((MX\|CLY)-)?\d+$`; links to `trade` | `"1003930"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].STATUS` | string | required | The trade's life-cycle status (NEW, VALIDATED, AMENDED,...), upper case. | one of `AMENDED`, `LIVE`, `NEW`, `VALIDATED` | `"AMENDED"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].PRODUCT` | string | required | The trade's product name (Calendar spread, Interest rate swap …). | — | `"ENGY-SWAP"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].ASSET_CLASS` | string | required | The trade's asset class (Rates, FX, Credit, Equity, Commodity, Inflation, Fixed income, Money market, Securities financing, Structured). | — | `"Commodity"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].CURRENCY` | string | required | The trade's currency, ISO 4217. | one of `AUD`, `CAD`, `CHF`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `JPY`, `USD` | `"USD"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].BOOK` | string | required | The book the trade is held in (a BOOK_ID of this pack). | — | `"BOOK-COMM-1"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].NOTIONAL` | number | required | The trade's notional, in the trade's own currency. | unit: trade currency | `10199198808.0` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].MATURITY` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The trade's maturity date. | — | `"2028-03-31"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].MATURITY_BUCKET` | string | required | The remaining maturity bucket of the trade: 0-1Y, 1-2Y, 2-5Y, 5-10Y or 10Y+. | one of `0-1Y`, `1-2Y`, `10Y+`, `2-5Y`, `5-10Y` | `"1-2Y"` |
| `TOP_TRADES[].MTM` | number | required | The trade's MTM, in the bank's reporting currency (USD in the demo). | unit: USD | `-120455169` |
| `DESK` | string | required | The desk the book sits under: a DESK_ID of the core pack's desk kind (DESK-…). | pattern `^DESK-`; links to `desk` | `"DESK-COMM"` |
| `ACCOUNTING_TREATMENT` | string | required | The accounting classification of the book's positions, e.g. Fair value (FVTPL). | — | `"Fair value (FVTPL)"` |
| `REGULATORY_BOOK` | string | required | Trading book or banking book, as the book is classified for regulatory capital. | — | `"Trading book"` |
| `VOLCKER` | string | required | The book's Volcker-rule permitted activity (e.g. Market making). | — | `"Market making"` |

### Fields in other rows

None: all 1,800 rows were read, and every field any of them has is in the record above.

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `BOOK_ID` per `business_date`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `BOOK_ID`, `NAME`, `DESK_NAME`, `TRADE_COUNT`, `MTM`, `DV01`, `TOP_TRADES`, `DESK`, `ACCOUNTING_TREATMENT`, `REGULATORY_BOOK`, `VOLCKER` (the contract's required fields).
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Each day: the records new or changed that day (or all of them); Drishti keeps the rest from the day before.
- Unique: `BOOK_ID` per business_date.
- `BOOK_ID` matches `^BOOK-`.
- `TRADE_COUNT` is at least 0.

## Holiday calendar: calendar (CAL)

Business-day calendar (USNY, TARGET, GBLO, JPTO…). One row per holiday calendar per business date, keyed by CALENDAR_ID. Read by the **core** pack's connector `reference-store` (table `<root>/reference/calendar/`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (4 records); the records never changed over the period, so every later day's file is empty. Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 4 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/core/calendar/` + `calendar.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `CALENDAR_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 4 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json
{
  "CALENDAR_ID": "CAL-GBLO",
  "NAME": "London",
  "HOLIDAYS": [
    {
      "DATE": "2026-01-01",
      "NAME": "New Year's Day",
      "WEEKDAY": "Thursday",
      "YEAR": 2026,
      "OBSERVED": ""
    },
    {
      "DATE": "2026-04-03",
      "NAME": "Good Friday",
      "WEEKDAY": "Friday",
      "YEAR": 2026,
      "OBSERVED": ""
    },
    "… 14 more elements of the same shape"
  ],
  "HOLIDAYS_2026": 8,
  "HOLIDAYS_2027": 8,
  "NEXT_HOLIDAY": "Christmas Day",
  "NEXT_HOLIDAY_DATE": "2026-12-25",
  "WEEKEND": [
    "Saturday",
    "Sunday"
  ]
}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CALENDAR_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^CAL-` | `"CAL-GBLO"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The calendar's name (TARGET2, New York, London, Tokyo). | — | `"London"` |
| `HOLIDAYS` | array of objects | required | The calendar's holidays of 2026 and 2027 in date order: one object per holiday. | — | [16 objects] |
| `HOLIDAYS[].DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The day the market is closed. | — | `"2026-01-01"` |
| `HOLIDAYS[].NAME` | string | required | The holiday's name (New Year's Day, Christmas Day …). | — | `"New Year's Day"` |
| `HOLIDAYS[].WEEKDAY` | string | required | The weekday of DATE, in English (Monday … Friday). | one of `Friday`, `Monday`, `Thursday`, `Tuesday`, `Wednesday` | `"Thursday"` |
| `HOLIDAYS[].YEAR` | integer | required | The year of the holiday (four digits). | seen: `2026`, `2027` | `2026` |
| `HOLIDAYS[].OBSERVED` | string | optional (filled in 11% of `HOLIDAYS[]` entries) | Yes when DATE is the observed (moved) day of a holiday that falls on a weekend; empty otherwise. | — | `"Yes"` |
| `HOLIDAYS_2026` | integer | required | How many holidays the calendar has in 2026 (weekends not counted). | — | `8` |
| `HOLIDAYS_2027` | integer | required | How many holidays the calendar has in 2027 (weekends not counted). | — | `8` |
| `NEXT_HOLIDAY` | string | required | The name of the next holiday after the data's date (none when there is none in the list). | — | `"Christmas Day"` |
| `NEXT_HOLIDAY_DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date of NEXT_HOLIDAY. | — | `"2026-12-25"` |
| `WEEKEND` | array of strings | required | The calendar's weekend days, by English day name (Saturday, Sunday); they are never business days. | — | [2 values] |

None: all 4 rows were read, and every field any of them has is in the record above.

- **Identity:** one record per `CALENDAR_ID` per `business_date`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `CALENDAR_ID`, `NAME`, `HOLIDAYS`, `HOLIDAYS_2026`, `HOLIDAYS_2027`, `NEXT_HOLIDAY`, `NEXT_HOLIDAY_DATE`, `WEEKEND` (the contract's required fields).
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Each day: the records new or changed that day (or all of them); Drishti keeps the rest from the day before.
- Unique: `CALENDAR_ID` per business_date.

Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 123 rows in all.

| Vector fields | none |

| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

<a id="counterparty"></a>

## Counterparty: counterparty (CPTY)

A legal entity the bank trades with: identifiers (LEI, UEN), rating, sector, country of risk and parent group. One row per counterparty per business date, keyed by COUNTERPARTY_ID. Read by the **core** pack's connector `reference-store` (table `<root>/reference/counterparty/`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (24 records); each later day's file holds only the records new or changed that day (24–24 a day). Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 1,440 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/core/counterparty/` + `counterparty.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `COUNTERPARTY_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `COUNTERPARTY_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^CP-` | `"CP-CASCADIA"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The counterparty's legal name. | — | `"Cascadia Airlines Inc."` |
| `LEI` | string | required | The counterparty's Legal Entity Identifier: 20 characters, ISO 17442. | — | `"5493005CUB4V16ZSQX54"` |
| `RATING` | string | required | The counterparty's credit rating, S&P-style (AA-, BBB+ …). | — | `"BB"` |
| `SECTOR` | string | required | The counterparty's industry sector (Pensions, Banking, Utilities …). | — | `"Airlines"` |
| `COUNTRY` | string | required | The counterparty's country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. | — | `"CA"` |
| `TYPE` | string | required | The kind of counterparty (Bank, Corporate, Hedge fund, Insurer, Pension fund …). | — | `"Corporate"` |
| `COUNTRY_OF_RISK` | string | required | The country of risk, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; trades carry the same value as COUNTERPARTY_COUNTRY_OF_RISK. | — | `"CA"` |
| `UEN` | string | required | The counterparty's unique entity number in the bank's client master (UEN and seven digits); trades carry it as COUNTERPARTY_UEN. | — | `"UEN0100148"` |
| `ECONOMY` | string | required | The economy of its country: an ECONOMY_ID of the world-economy pack's economy kind (ECON- and the ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code). | pattern `^ECON-`; links to `economy` | `"ECON-CAN"` |
| `NEWS_ID` | string | required | Its headlines: a NEWS_ID of the news-and-markets pack's news kind (NEWS- and the name with underscores). | pattern `^NEWS-`; links to `news` | `"NEWS-Cascadia_Airlines_Inc."` |
| `NET_MTM` | number | required | The sum of the NET_MTM of its netting sets, in the bank's reporting currency (USD in the demo); positive when the counterparty owes the bank. | unit: USD | `400541282.366474` |
| `NETTING_SETS` | array of objects | required | The counterparty's netting sets: one object per netting set. | links to `netting-set` | [4 objects] |
| `NETTING_SETS[].ID` | string | required | The netting set: a NETTING_SET_ID of the counterparty-risk pack's netting-set kind (NS-…). | — | `"NS-CASCADIA-FRA"` |
| `NETTING_SETS[].AGREEMENT` | string | required | The master agreement governing it: an AGREEMENT_ID of the counterparty-risk pack's agreement kind (AGR-…). | pattern `^AGR-`; links to `agreement` | `"AGR-CASCADIA-ISDA"` |
| `NETTING_SETS[].TRADES` | integer | required | How many trades the netting set holds. | — | `29` |
| `NETTING_SETS[].NET_MTM` | number | required | The netting set's net MTM, in the bank's reporting currency (USD in the demo); positive when the counterparty owes the bank. | unit: USD | `12205330.366592` |
| `KYC` | object | required | The counterparty's know-your-customer record: one object. | — | {…} |
| `KYC.STATUS` | string | required | The KYC review's outcome (Approved …). | — | `"Approved"` |
| `KYC.RISK_RATING` | string | required | The KYC risk rating: Standard for a counterparty rated A or better, Enhanced otherwise. | one of `Enhanced`, `Standard` | `"Enhanced"` |
| `KYC.LAST_REVIEW` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The date of the last KYC review. | — | `"2026-02-11"` |
| `KYC.EMIR_CLASSIFICATION` | string | required | The counterparty's EMIR class: FC (financial counterparty) or NFC- (non-financial below the clearing threshold). | one of `FC`, `NFC-` | `"NFC-"` |
| `KYC.PD_1Y` | number | required | The one-year probability of default implied by RATING, as a fraction (0.0004 is 0.04%). | unit: fraction | `0.0068` |
| `GROUP` | string | required | The group it belongs to: a GROUP_ID of the core pack's counterparty-group kind (GRP-…). | pattern `^GRP-`; links to `counterparty-group` | `"GRP-CASCADIA"` |
| `CREDIT_LIMIT` | string | required | Its credit limit: a LIMIT_ID of the counterparty-risk pack's credit-limit kind (LIM-…). | pattern `^LIM-`; links to `credit-limit` | `"LIM-CASCADIA"` |
| `HIERARCHY` | object | required | The counterparty in its legal hierarchy, as a graph: its group over its members, and under it its agreement, CSA and netting sets. | — | {…} |
| `HIERARCHY.NODES` | array of objects | required | The graph's nodes: one object per entity (the group, its counterparties, the agreement, the CSA, the netting sets). | — | [11 objects] |
| `HIERARCHY.NODES[].ID` | string | required | The node's entity id: a group (GRP-), counterparty (CP-), agreement (AGR-), CSA (CSA-) or netting set (NS-). | — | `"GRP-CASCADIA"` |
| `HIERARCHY.NODES[].LABEL` | string | required | The node's display name (for a netting set its id and trade count). | — | `"Cascadia Airlines Inc."` |
| `HIERARCHY.NODES[].TYPE` | string | required | What the node is: Group (ultimate parent), Counterparty, Agreement, CSA or Netting set. | one of `Agreement`, `CSA`, `Counterparty`, `Group (ultimate parent)`, `Netting set` | `"Group (ultimate parent)"` |
| `HIERARCHY.EDGES` | array of objects | required | The graph's edges: one object per link between two nodes (parent of, signed, secured by, nets, governs). | — | [14 objects] |
| `HIERARCHY.EDGES[].FROM` | string | required | The parent node's id (a NODES[].ID). | — | `"GRP-CASCADIA"` |
| `HIERARCHY.EDGES[].TO` | string | required | The child node's id (a NODES[].ID). | — | `"CP-CASCADIA"` |
| `HIERARCHY.EDGES[].LABEL` | string | required | How FROM relates to TO: parent of (group to member), signed (counterparty to ISDA), secured by (ISDA to each CSA, one per bank legal entity), nets (ISDA to netting set), governs (CSA to the netting set it margins). | one of `governs`, `nets`, `parent of`, `secured by`, `signed` | `"parent of"` |
| `CREDIT_CURVE` | string | optional (filled in 29% of rows) | Its CDS curve, when it is also a bond issuer: a CURVE_ID of the market-data pack's credit-curve kind (CDS-…). | pattern `^CDS-`; links to `credit-curve` | `"CDS-CASCADIA"` |
| `LEGAL_ENTITY` | string | optional (filled in every row) | The bank's legal entity that faces it: an ENTITY_ID of the core pack's legal-entity kind (LE-…). | pattern `^LE-`; links to `legal-entity` | `"LE-NY"` |

- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Each day: the records new or changed that day (or all of them); Drishti keeps the rest from the day before.
- Unique: `DESK_ID` per business_date.
- `DESK_ID` matches `^DESK-`.

<a id="issuer"></a>

## Issuer: issuer (ISS)

Issuer of bonds and reference entity for CDS. One row per issuer per business date, keyed by ISSUER_ID. Read by the **core** pack's connector `reference-store` (table `<root>/reference/issuer/`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (16 records); the records never changed over the period, so every later day's file is empty. Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 16 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/core/issuer/` + `issuer.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `ISSUER_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 16 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json
{
  "ISSUER_ID": "ISS-CASCADIA",
  "NAME": "Cascadia Airlines Inc.",
  "RATING": "BB",
  "SECTOR": "Airlines",
  "COUNTRY": "CA",
  "BONDS": [
    {
      "ISIN": "CACASC059511",
      "COUPON": 0.0552,
      "MATURITY": "2031-02-15"
    },
    {
      "ISIN": "CACASC169344",
      "COUPON": 0.0602,
      "MATURITY": "2036-01-15"
    }
  ],
  "CREDIT_CURVE": "CDS-CASCADIA",
  "LEI": "5493005CUB4V16ZSQX54",
  "EQUITY": "EQ-CSCA"
}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ISSUER_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^ISS-` | `"ISS-CASCADIA"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The issuer's legal name. | — | `"Cascadia Airlines Inc."` |
| `RATING` | string | required | The issuer's credit rating, S&P-style (AAA, BBB- …). | — | `"BB"` |
| `SECTOR` | string | required | The issuer's sector (Sovereign, Banking, Airlines …). | — | `"Airlines"` |
| `COUNTRY` | string | required | The issuer's country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. | — | `"CA"` |
| `BONDS` | array of objects | required | The issuer's bonds: one object per bond. | — | [2 objects] |
| `BONDS[].ISIN` | string | required | The bond's ISIN, 12 characters (without the BND- prefix of the market-data pack's bond id). | — | `"CACASC059511"` |
| `BONDS[].COUPON` | number | required | The bond's annual coupon rate, as a fraction (0.038 is 3.8%). | unit: fraction | `0.0552` |
| `BONDS[].MATURITY` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The bond's maturity date. | — | `"2031-02-15"` |
| `CREDIT_CURVE` | string | required | The issuer's CDS curve: a CURVE_ID of the market-data pack's credit-curve kind (CDS-…). | pattern `^CDS-`; links to `credit-curve` | `"CDS-CASCADIA"` |
| `LEI` | string | required | The issuer's Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442, 20 characters); synthetic in the test data. | — | `"5493005CUB4V16ZSQX54"` |
| `EQUITY` | string | optional (filled in 62% of rows) | The issuer's listed share, when it has one: a TICKER of the market-data pack's equity kind (EQ-…). | pattern `^EQ-`; links to `equity` | `"EQ-CSCA"` |

- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Each day: the records new or changed that day (or all of them); Drishti keeps the rest from the day before.
- Unique: `ISSUER_ID` per business_date.
- `ISSUER_ID` matches `^ISS-`.

## Bank legal entity: legal-entity (LE)

The bank's own booking entity. One row per bank legal entity per business date, keyed by ENTITY_ID. Read by the **core** pack's connector `reference-store` (table `<root>/reference/legal-entity/`). Delivered **daily**, 60 business days (2026-07-08 to 2026-09-30): the first day's file is a **full snapshot** (4 records); each later day's file holds only the records new or changed that day (4–4 a day). Drishti applies a day's file by key over the day before: a record absent from a day's file keeps its previous version, and nothing is ever deleted (an end is a changed status). 240 rows in all.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/core/legal-entity/` + `legal-entity.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `ENTITY_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the business date is the file's date (`<table>.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz`), which becomes the lake's partition `business_date` |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | a full snapshot on the first day, then only the changed records |

A real record, the most complete of the 240 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

    },

    }
  ]

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ENTITY_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^LE-` | `"LE-FRA"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The legal entity's registered name. | one of `Drishti Bank Europe AG`, `Drishti Bank Securities Inc.`, `Drishti Bank plc`, `Drishti Securities Japan K.K.` | `"Drishti Bank Europe AG"` |
| `LEI` | string | required | The entity's Legal Entity Identifier: 20 characters, ISO 17442. | one of `549300BLAOJ55ZE6F474`, `549300O1N13GO2II2096`, `549300Z8F6KKOGHS7Q83`, `549300Z9DXU4T18OK744` | `"549300Z9DXU4T18OK744"` |
| `JURISDICTION` | string | required | The country the entity is incorporated and regulated in, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. | links to `jurisdiction` | `"DE"` |
| `REGULATOR` | string | required | The entity's prudential and conduct regulators, separated by ' / ' (ECB / BaFin, PRA / FCA …). | one of `ECB / BaFin`, `JFSA`, `PRA / FCA`, `SEC / CFTC / FINRA` | `"ECB / BaFin"` |
| `DESKS` | array of objects | required | The desks that book in the entity: one object per desk. | — | [1 objects] |
| `DESKS[].ID` | string | required | The desk: a DESK_ID of the core pack's desk kind (DESK-…). | — | `"DESK-SFT"` |
| `DESKS[].NAME` | string | required | The desk's name (its desk NAME). | — | `"Repo and securities lending"` |
| `BOOKS` | array of objects | required | The books of those desks that hold trades: one object per book, with its P&L, MTM and trade count. | — | [3 objects] |
| `BOOKS[].BOOK` | string | required | The book: a BOOK_ID of the core pack's book kind (BOOK-…). | pattern `^BOOK-`; links to `book` | `"BOOK-SFT-1"` |
| `BOOKS[].DESK` | string | required | The NAME of the book's desk (a name such as Repo and securities lending, not a DESK_ID, although the contract links it to desk). | links to `desk` | `"Repo and securities lending"` |
| `BOOKS[].PNL` | integer | required | The book's one-day P&L: the sum of its trades' PNL_1D, gain positive. | unit: USD | `-11770547` |
| `BOOKS[].MTM` | integer | required | The book's mark to market: the sum of its trades' MTM, from the bank's side (positive is owed to the bank). | unit: USD | `337967490` |
| `BOOKS[].TRADES` | integer | required | The number of trades in the book. | — | `243` |
